elements.evidence: The added clause states that “IBM may terminate this Agreement, any Statement of Work or Product Attachment, in whole or in part, for its convenience.”

elements.element: Customer’s termination-for-convenience right is exercisable on thirty (30) days’ prior written notice.
elements.evidence: The added clause expressly requires “thirty (30) days’ prior written notice to MSL.”

elements.element: Upon Customer’s termination for convenience, Vendor must provide a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees attributable to the period after termination becomes effective.
elements.evidence: MSL must “refund to IBM any amounts prepaid by IBM for the period after the effective date of termination,” which provides the required refund of the unused prepaid period.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: The clause states that “MSL shall have no right to terminate this Agreement, any Statement of Work or any Product Attachment for convenience prior to the end of the then current term.”
IBM is expressly permitted to terminate the Agreement, Statements of Work, and Product Attachments for convenience.

elements.element: Customer’s termination-for-convenience right is exercisable on 60–90 days’ notice.
elements.evidence: The operative notice period is thirty (30) days, not a period within the required 60–90-day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee imposed on Customer for termination for convenience does not exceed three months’ fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed: IBM “shall not be liable for any termination charge, penalty or other payment by reason of such termination,” apart from ordinary amounts payable for Products and Parts under Sections 5.2 and 5.3. Thus, the applicable early-termination fee is zero.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The original renewal language allows either Party to give notice of its intent to terminate rather than renew, while the added clause restricts MSL only “prior to the end of the then current term.” Read together, MSL retains an end-of-term termination/nonrenewal right.

elements.element: Vendor may not terminate for convenience before the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The added clause expressly provides that MSL has no termination-for-convenience right “prior to the end of the then current term.”

elements.element: Vendor’s end-of-term termination-for-convenience right requires ninety (90) days’ notice.
elements.evidence: No 90-day notice right is provided. The Agreement requires six (6) months’ notice, and the Attachment requires twelve (12) months’ notice.

result.reason: The operative language fully satisfies the preferred position, including IBM’s 30-day written-notice right, refund of unused prepaid amounts, and prohibition on MSL’s mid-term convenience termination. The fallback fails because its specified Customer and Vendor notice periods are not provided. The redline is not minimal because it also inserts an unrelated Parts-pricing provision and expands the convenience right to partial terminations and subsidiary documents. The targeted termination changes use a notwithstanding clause and preserve the existing cause, payment, term, and renewal provisions without an unresolved contradiction, but the unrelated pricing paragraph, placeholder, typo, and awkward placement reduce drafting quality.
